extracted.intended_audience: Participating Agencies, SBIR/STTR program managers, SBA staff, and policy stakeholders involved in SBIR/STTR compliance and reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and metrics for evaluating agency compliance with SBIR/STTR statutory requirements, award-size policies, proposal selection metrics, award timelines, and geographical distribution reporting for FY22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum SBIR spending requirement (3.2%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Agencies must obligate a minimum of 3.2% of extramural R/R&D reported to SBA for SBIR activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA assesses compliance against extramural R/R&D reported to SBA (minus exemptions). DoD multi-year appropriations and obligations across fiscal years can affect compliance calculations; SBA may perform retrospective analyses by appropriation year (e.g., FY21 appropriation obligated in FY21 and FY22) to clarify compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum STTR spending requirement (0.45%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Agencies must obligate a minimum of 0.45% of extramural R/R&D reported to SBA for STTR activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same calculation considerations as SBIR (exemptions, reporting of extramural R/R&D, multi-year obligations). SBA retrospective tables compare appropriation-year obligations to extramural R/R&D to compute percentage compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation-year vs obligation-year reporting rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may report the year of funding (appropriation year) with the year funds were obligated when uploading awards to SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because RDT&E appropriations may be available for obligations over two years and agencies reserve funds across years, SBA allows reporting of appropriation year alongside obligation year. SBA uses this data to produce retrospective comparisons (e.g., FY21 appropriation obligations obligated in FY21 and FY22) to assess compliance with minimum set-asides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting multi-year obligations in compliance determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD and other agencies may obligate appropriated funds across the appropriated FY and the subsequent FY; SBA accounts for this in compliance assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department executes authorized SBIR/STTR funding over two years; SBA will consider obligated funds by appropriation year in retrospective analyses to determine whether components meet minimum set-aside percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory guideline award amounts (baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Small Business Act guideline award parameters: Phase I at $150,000 and Phase II at $1,000,000 (statutory baselines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies historically solicit awards at or below these guidelines depending on budget and policy objectives. The statute permits agencies to request waivers to exceed these guidelines under specified procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed exceedance of guideline amounts (up to 50%) and inflation adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: An Agency may, at its discretion, exceed the guideline amounts by up to 50%, making effective maximums $225,000 for Phase I and $1.5 million for Phase II; amounts are adjusted every year for inflation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY22, inflation-adjusted thresholds (without SBA waiver) were $275,765 for Phase I and $1,838,436 for Phase II. Any award above those FY-specific thresholds requires an SBA waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for SBA waiver when exceeding inflation-adjusted thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Any award above the inflation-adjusted maximum award amounts (the guideline + allowable adjustment) requires a waiver from SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only agencies that obtained SBA waivers (e.g., DoD, HHS, NASA in FY22) may make awards above those thresholds. Agencies must follow Section 7(i)(4) of the SBIR/STTR Policy Directive when requesting waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in waiver requests (Section 7(i)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency requesting a waiver to exceed the award cap must provide to SBA: (1) evidence that limitations on award size interfere with the agency's ability to fulfill its R&D mission; (2) evidence that the agency will minimize, to the maximum extent practicable, the number of awards that exceed the cap for the topic area; and (3) evidence that research costs for the topic area differ significantly from those in other areas to warrant going over the cap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must substantiate waiver requests with programmatic and cost evidence. SBA expects documentation demonstrating mission impact, minimization strategies, and cost differentials by topic area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of awards above cap (identity and location)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must report to SBA any awards made that exceed the cap, including the identity and location of each awardee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA requires reporting of awards that exceed guideline thresholds so it can monitor waiver usage and the distribution of such awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justifications for HHS/NIH larger awards (biomedical guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH/HHS may request waivers for specific biomedical topics because life science SBIR/STTR projects often require funding above statutory guidelines to enable commercialization and regulatory progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifications include: high cost of early-stage biomedical/behavioral research, need for pre-clinical development, regulatory filings/testing/approval costs, extensive third-party funding/partnership requirements, and long timelines and high ultimate costs to reach market. HHS contends underfunding Phase I/II/IIB projects may cause failure to reach marketplace and impede mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justifications for DoD larger awards
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD typically requests waivers for contract-specific critical technology projects requiring additional investment to meet technology readiness levels (TRLs) or to spur accelerated development through pilot topics and Phase III funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD waiver requests are often targeted to specific critical technology or pilot topic projects where extra SBIR/STTR investment is necessary to meet programmatic TRL goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justifications for NASA larger awards
rubrics_metrics.description: NASA has requested waivers to offer sequential Phase II awards that exceed guidelines to meet nearer-term technology needs for initiatives (e.g., Moon to Mars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mission-driven justifications demonstrating need for phased or sequential funding beyond guideline amounts to meet agency-specific objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of proposal selection rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal selection rate = number of awards made divided by the total number of proposals received within the fiscal year; SBA monitors selection rates for Phase I and Phase II awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY22 program-wide Phase I selection rate example: 3,859 Phase I awards selected from 21,911 Phase I proposals = 17.6%. Agencies also report percent of Phase I winners that are first-time winners (e.g., 39% in FY22). Selection rates are tracked by agency and program (SBIR vs STTR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking and reporting of multiple award winners (>15 Phase IIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must track Phase II awards made to companies that received more than 15 Phase II awards during the preceding five fiscal years (FY17–FY21) and report counts and shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables report number of such companies, number of Phase II awards they received, percentage of Phase II companies who are multiple award winners, and how many FY22 Phase I awards those companies received. This metric monitors concentration of awards among prolific winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy Directive timelines for solicitation-to-notification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Policy Directive prescribes maximum durations between solicitation close and notification of recommendation of award: not more than one year (<= 1 year) for NIH and NSF; not more than 90 calendar days for all other agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA expects agencies to meet these timeline requirements and reports percent of awards meeting the thresholds. DoD and civilian agencies report compliance rates by component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy Directive timelines for solicitation-to-performance start
rubrics_metrics.description: The Policy Directive prescribes maximum durations between solicitation close and the first date of the period of performance: not more than 15 months for NIH and NSF; not more than 180 calendar days for all other agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should ensure award start dates meet these caps; SBA reports percentages of awards meeting the requirement and average days between solicitation close and performance start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award timeline performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeline metrics to monitor include: average time between solicitation close and award notification; average time between notification and first day of performance; percentage of awards meeting the notification and performance-start thresholds; average time between Phase I award final day and Phase II award first day; average Phase II solicitation close (or proposal receipt) to award notification; average Phase II notification to performance start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA publishes these averages and percentages by agency and component (civilian, DoD service agencies, ODAs). Note: HHS and DOE Phase II timelines may include Fast-Track projects which use Phase I solicitation close date and can increase averages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data provenance and updateability guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeline and award-count/dollar data originate from Participating Agencies' uploads to SBA; agencies can update numbers and dollar amounts on SBIR.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tables reflect snapshots in time (e.g., retrieved September 13, 2023). SBA notes that award counts are only for new awards during FY22 while dollar obligations include funding for new and prior-year awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic distribution monitoring and outreach guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA monitors SBIR/STTR award distribution by state and territory and notes concentration of funding in states with large populations or strong R&D histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately 68% of FY22 SBIR dollars and 63% of FY22 STTR dollars went to a set of high-receipt states. SBA and agencies coordinate outreach with economic development agencies, universities, accelerators, and local small business service providers to foster participation in underrepresented regions.
